newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish mobile phone firm sees 40 pct market share.
newsitem.headline: Polish mobile phone firm sees 40 pct market share.

text.p: The cellular telephone consortium of Polish and foreign firms Polkomtel SA, which launches services on Tuesday, expects to take a market share of over 40 percent in about a year, the company's President said.
Polkomtel is Poland's third mobile phone operator, following analogue Centertel SA and GSM firm PTC Era GSM SA, which started operations earlier this month.
"I think the two GSM firms can take 40-something percent of the market each, with analogue Centertel taking the rest," Wladyslaw Bartoszewicz told a news conference on Monday.

Danish telecom operator Tele Danmark and U.S. AirTouch Communications each hold a 19.25-percent stake of Polkomtel, which seeks to provide services to more than 30 Polish cities and attract at least 30,000 customers by year-end.
It would cover a geographic area containing 37 percent of the country's population.
It plans to provide services to at least 100,000 customers by the end of 1997, covering 80 percent of Poland's inhabitants, and to become available to 90 percent of the population by mid-1998.
By the end of the week its customers will be able to call Denmark, Holland, Switzerland, Finland, Britain and the Czech Republic.
The firm, which calls its Polish network "Plus GSM", has said it will invest $1 billion by the year 2000 to attract one million customers.
Bartoszewicz said Polkomtel was still negotiating with state telecom monopoly Telekomunikacja Polska SA to forge an agreement on sharing revenue from calls between Polkomtel and TPSA network.
TPSA owns half of Centertel, with France Telecom and Ameritech Corp holding the rest. The consortium, active since 1991, provides services to more tha 100,000 customers.
Polkomtel also groups Polish copper combine KGHM SA, Plock oil refinery and the National Power Grid (PSE).

Era's shoreholders include US West of the United States and Deutsche Telekom's subsidiary DeTeMobil, with 22.5-percent stakes each, and Polish conglomerate Elektrim SA, which controls 32.5 percent of shares.
